comparison: Both evaluate the emergence of place-like and border-like cells (C9, C10, C40, C49, C50, C52, C80). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of visual evidence and characterization, while peer reviewers consistently affirm these findings as 'solid,' 'clearly described,' and 'convincing.' Strong agreement on core computational results.

Both address global remapping findings (C11, C55-C57, C63-C65, C81). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with detailed quantitative analysis, peer reviewers explicitly state remapping is 'convincing and well-supported' and 'thorough and interesting.' OpenEval also covers mechanistic basis (C45, C58-C62, C82) which peers acknowledge. Strong agreement.

OpenEval R4 addresses mechanistic basis of remapping (C12, C45, C58-C62, C82, C152), which overlaps with peer R2's evaluation of remapping. Both find evidence SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes the mechanistic link is 'somewhat inferential.' Peers praise thoroughness without raising concerns about inference.

Perfect claim overlap on geometric manipulation responses (C83-C95). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes findings are primarily visual inspection, peers describe as 'interesting' and 'strong evidence for map-like generalisation.' Complete agreement on this result.

Both address hexagonal arrangement of place field centers (C14, C43, C131-C134). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED based on visual evidence, peers call it 'intriguing' and 'striking and potentially very interesting.' Both acknowledge finding is based on visual inspection rather than quantitative hexagonality metrics. Agreement on computational finding.

Both evaluate experimental mouse data analysis (C15, C144-C148, C150, C194). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN citing limited sample size and marginal significance, peers note the link 'may benefit from further development' and findings 'doesn't robustly support the modelling results.' Strong agreement on uncertainty and preliminary nature.

Both address noise injection and attractor dynamics (C99-C104). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of 'approximate attractor' terminology, peers describe stability as 'impressive' without criticism. Also covers stability findings (C121-C122). Agreement on support.

OpenEval R12 addresses UMAP dimensionality reduction (C106-C108), OpenEval R13 addresses PCA (C112-C118), both map to peer R8 which acknowledges low-dimensional projection analyses showing environment-specific structure. All mark SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes sensitivity to hyperparameters.

Both address PCA and dimensionality findings (C112-C118). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of explained variance and factorization, peers acknowledge the analysis without criticism. Agreement on support for representational structure findings.

Both address context signal mechanism (C126-C128). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED noting speculative but plausible mechanistic interpretation, peers describe remapping analysis including context mechanism as 'thorough and interesting' without challenge. Also covers C105, C125 on context mismatch.

Both reference context mismatch experiments (C105, C125). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN because supporting data not shown in reviewed material, peers acknowledge as part of remapping mechanism without specific evaluation. Limited basis for comparison.

Both address absence of grid cells and path integration capability (C13, C41, C137, C170, C184). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED as well-documented negative result, peers acknowledge as 'interesting possibility' but note 'role of grid cells...remains elusive' and integration with broader picture unclear. Agreement on finding, divergence on implications.

Both address interpretive claims about grid cells and path integration (C42, C175-C176, C186-C187). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED noting appropriate framing as questions rather than conclusions, peers acknowledge interest but note implications need further development. Agreement that claims are interpretive.

Both address interpretation connecting absence of grid cells to hexagonal place field arrangement (C44, C138, C193). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED noting tentative language, peers find hexagonal pattern 'intriguing' and potentially related to optimal coverage. Agreement on interpretation being plausible but not definitively tested.

Both address prediction about rate remapping in CA1 (C151-C155) and alternative mechanisms (C156-C157, C159). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED for prediction, UNCERTAIN for alternatives; peers mark UNCERTAIN noting mechanisms are 'plausible' but role of grid cells 'remains elusive.' Agreement on uncertainty about broader implications.

Both address acknowledged model limitations regarding field doubling (C161-C165). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED for the limitation acknowledgment and proposed explanation, peers do not challenge these limitations. Agreement on transparent discussion of model constraints.

Both address limitations regarding multiple fields during expansion (C166-C169). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED for limitation and mechanistic explanation, peers acknowledge model choices may not fully reflect biological reality. Agreement on limitation acknowledgment.

Both address speculative alternative mechanisms (C156-C159). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN noting these are untested hypotheses, peers similarly note mechanisms are plausible but integration with broader picture remains elusive. Agreement on speculative nature.

Perfect claim overlap on speculative mechanistic model connecting border, place, and grid cells (C196-C204). Both mark UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes creative hypothesis but primarily theoretical speculation, peers state role of grid cells and integration 'remains elusive.' Complete agreement on uncertainty.

OpenEval R14 addresses eigenvalue analysis and stability (C119-C124, including C121-C122), peer R7 addresses noise injection stability. Both note impressive stability despite theoretical concerns. Partial overlap on stability observations.

OpenEval R28 addresses clustering near borders in model and data (C139-C140), peer R6 addresses experimental data analysis more broadly (C139, C144-C150). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED for clustering observation, peers mark experimental comparison as UNCERTAIN. Partial agreement on clustering, divergence on experimental validation strength.

OpenEval evaluates core methodological innovation and model architecture (C6-C8, C32). No corresponding specific peer evaluation found, though peers generally acknowledge model is 'clearly described.' Methodological details not specifically challenged.

OpenEval evaluates rate overlap and difference analyses (C67-C74) showing bimodal distributions. No specific corresponding peer evaluation, though these analyses support remapping findings that peers endorse. Technical analysis not separately evaluated by peers.

OpenEval evaluates population vector correlation analysis (C75-C79). No specific corresponding peer evaluation, though this provides population-level evidence for remapping that peers support. Technical analysis not separately evaluated.
OpenEval evaluates training performance and convergence (C47-C48). No corresponding peer evaluation found. Basic training results not specifically discussed by peers.
OpenEval evaluates sparsity of representations (C53-C54). No corresponding peer evaluation found. Technical characteristic not separately evaluated by peers.
OpenEval evaluates specific testable prediction about center-surround profile (C96). No corresponding peer evaluation found. Specific prediction not separately discussed by peers.
OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN for speculative interpretations of dimensionality reduction (C109-C111). No corresponding peer evaluation found. Interpretive claims not separately evaluated.
OpenEval evaluates methodological observation about hexagonal pattern clarity with aggregation (C141). No corresponding peer evaluation found. Methodological detail not separately discussed.

OpenEval evaluates analysis of place field center transformations between environments (C142-C143). No corresponding peer evaluation found. Technical analysis supporting remapping not separately evaluated.
